CausalChain: Hypoxia leads to HIF activation -> Upregulation of glycolytic enzymes (e.g., HK2, LDHA) elevates lactate production -> Excess lactate acidifies the tumor microenvironment and signals via lactate receptors (e.g., GPR81) -> Lactate drives polarization of macrophages to an M2 phenotype -> M2 macrophages secrete cytokines that stimulate the serine synthesis pathway (e.g., PHGDH upregulation) in tumor cells -> Enhanced NADPH production and redox homeostasis support survival and drug resistance.
Hypothesis: In hypoxic hepatocellular carcinoma, lactate-driven M2 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages induces a paracrine upregulation of the serine synthesis pathway in cancer cells, thereby enhancing NADPH-dependent redox balance and contributing to TKI and ICI resistance. Targeting either the lactate-mediated macrophage signaling or the downstream serine metabolism can disrupt this feedback loop and sensitize HCC cells to therapy.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumors are characterized by a hypoxic microenvironment that drives profound metabolic reprogramming through hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs). This reprogramming not only shifts energy production from mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis – leading to an accumulation of lactate – but also establishes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment via adenosinergic signaling and altered immune cell recruitment. We propose that the lactate produced by HIF-driven glycolysis actively polarizes tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) toward an M2 phenotype, which then secrete cytokines and growth factors that in turn stimulate the serine synthesis pathway (SSP) in HCC cells. The resultant upregulation of enzymes such as PHGDH increases NADPH production and bolsters redox homeostasis, thereby enhancing the survival of HCC cells and promoting resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This intercellular metabolic crosstalk represents a potentially targetable feed-forward loop to overcome drug resistance in hypoxic HCC.
